# Fanfarr v0.5.19

Fanfarr finds theme music for a Plex library, writes it beside the media as a
local `theme.mp3`, and keeps a permanent record of what it did and why.

## The eMudhra CA compromise

In October 2026, eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authorities turned out
to have private keys recoverable from their public certificates, so anyone could
mint certificates that validate against the roots those intermediates chain to.
Clients that do not consume revocation or Certificate Transparency data get no
signal from that. Erlang's TLS client is such a client -- and it is what this
app talks to Plex, ThemerrDB and poster hosts with -- so the only protection
that exists is the root leaving the trust store.

Two of the affected roots ship in Debian bookworm, which this image is built on,
and Debian has no fixed package for bookworm yet. The image now removes them
itself, using the mechanism Debian documents: `emSign ECC Root CA - C3` and
`emSign Root CA - C1`, taking the bundle from 148 certificates to 146.

`emSign Root CA - G1` is deliberately kept -- eMudhra states it is not being
removed -- and `G3` and the AAA cross-sign were never in this store.

Verified in the published image rather than inferred: both roots are absent by
byte match, a control root is present to prove that check works, and Erlang
reports the same 146 certificates at runtime.

The build also asserts its own patterns matched. A future `ca-certificates`
package that renames those files fails the build instead of quietly shipping the
trust this fix removes.

## Dependency advisories

A batch was published after the previous release and was caught by the audit
step that runs in the local gate and in CI:

- `bandit` 1.14.0 -- six advisories, four HIGH, all in the web server: HTTP/2
  stream recovery bypassing per-connection limits, quadratic bignum parsing of
  `Content-Length` and `Host` port values, 1-byte chunked bodies amplifying
  memory, WebSocket continuation frames bypassing the fragment limit, CR/LF in
  chunk extensions enabling request smuggling, and `WINDOW_UPDATE` frames
  resetting the body read timeout.
- `ash` 3.37.2 -- an upsert on a primary key ignoring attribute multitenancy.
  This app has no multitenancy, so it was not reachable here.
- `jose` 1.11.13 -- eight advisories, including ECDSA signature malleability.

## yt-dlp, and one accepted limitation

`yt-dlp` moves to 2026.10.21. Its certificate store is a separate story the
image cannot patch, and it is documented rather than glossed over: the binary
carries `certifi` and loads it explicitly, so the system store above does not
apply to it, and the version it currently bundles still trusts both removed
roots. It sends no credentials on that path, so the reachable impact is a
substituted audio file, while everything Fanfarr itself talks to uses the
patched store. The Dockerfile and the README both record the condition for
revisiting.

## Upgrading

Pull the new image and restart; the database migrates itself on boot.
